content_html:
Computational Neuroscience Models

This document places major families of computational neuroscience models on a single map and shows how each contributes to memory. It includes a matrix for quick lookup, a brief conceptual synthesis, and an APA-styled reference list with links.

Mechanism → Dynamics → Inference → Systems: Single-neuron and plasticity rules specify the mechanisms; population models and recurrent networks describe emergent dynamics; Bayesian and predictive-coding approaches frame memory as inference; CLS, graph models, and deep nets align with systems-level function and behavior.

In fluid terms: mechanisms are like micro-scale viscosity and boundary conditions; population dynamics define flow regimes; inference tunes pressure gradients; systems-level models route flows between reservoirs and channels.

Model Family What it Captures Core Math/Tooling Memory Angle Fluid-Mechanics Analogy
Single-Neuron (HH, LIF) Spiking, excitability, resonance ODEs; conductances; thresholds Temporal precision; phase-locking Local micro-currents; wave onset
Synaptic Plasticity (Hebb, STDP) Learning rules; consolidation Δw ∝ pre×post; timing kernels Trace formation; sequence linking Viscosity change in channels
Population / Rate (Wilson–Cowan) Mean-field activity; stability Coupled nonlinear ODEs; fields Attractors; oscillations Continuum flow; laminar regimes
Recurrent / Attractor (Hopfield; CANN) Content-addressable memory Energy landscapes; symmetry Pattern completion; working memory Vortices/eddies = stable states
Oscillations & Replay Theta–gamma; sleep/awake replay Coupled oscillators; traveling waves Consolidation; planning; binding Standing waves; waveguides
Bayesian / Predictive Coding / FEP Inference under uncertainty Generative models; variational bounds Reconstruction; priors × evidence Pressure gradients; flow optimization
Complementary Learning Systems (CLS) Hippocampus fast / cortex slow Dual-store; interleaved training Episodic→semantic consolidation Reservoir exchange; mixing layers
Graph / Semantic Networks Associative structure; search Random walks; diffusion; centrality Spreading activation; priming Diffusion in porous media
Deep Learning Inspired (Goal-driven, TEM) Task optimization; representation Gradient descent; attention; recurrence Generalization; sequence memory Tuned flow channels; valves (gates)
